A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same data engine, benchmark and model, renamed from DOGE to DOGR. Their complete main texts, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on DOGE-Bench, ten general document benchmarks, DocLocal4K and DOGE-Local15k, together with ablations and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds baseline comparisons, instruction-tuning and annotation-quality ablations, IoU sensitivity results and baseline failure examples.

M1.justification: The re-rendering, annotation merging and post-annotation procedures remain unchanged, as do the InternViT/Qwen2 architecture, three-stage training and coordinate representation. Renaming DOGE to DOGR and adding filtering explanations do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Benchmark evaluation coverage contracts: v2 Figure 4 and Table 2 omit posters from the three combined grounding-and-referring tasks evaluated in v1 Table 2. Poster training data remain, and the other document domains, DocLocal4K, Local15k and ten general benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds eleven competing models to DOGR-Bench, where v1 reported only DOGE, and seven MLLM comparators to DocLocal4K. These include GPT-4o, Gemini, Qwen-VL and InternVL variants. Table 3 additionally introduces Qwen2-VL-7B while removing eight older comparators, including Donut, UReader, TokenPacker and QwenVL.

E3.justification: The benchmark changes from 4,144 samples in v1 Table 1 to 3,600 with revised category proportions in v2 Section 4. New comparisons evaluate F1all at IoU 0.1, retain a DOGR row at 0.5 and examine thresholds in Figure 14. New ablations introduce instruction-data controls, 25k-sample generator comparisons and bounding-box perturbations within 30%; the previous tile-count experiment is removed.

E4.justification: v2 adds instruction-tuning data ablation, GPT-4o versus Gemini-generated training-data comparison, accurate versus perturbed bounding-box analysis, IoU sensitivity and baseline grounding failure cases. It removes v1's training/inference tile-count sensitivity study. The parsing-data ablations and existing qualitative examples remain.

E5.justification: New Figure 16 explicitly displays three attempts at the same InternVL2.5-72B grounding query, providing limited repeated-inference evidence of output variability. Neither version provides benchmark-level repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the original benchmark scores with revised results and extensive comparator entries; overall referring accuracy changes from 50.9 to 60.3 under the changed benchmark composition, so this is not an established same-setting gain. New ablation and sensitivity results are added, while tile-count results disappear. The proposed model's ten general-benchmark scores, retained DocLocal4K entries and Local15k Table 8 results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs, and the seven-task taxonomy and underlying mathematical descriptions remain unchanged. The added IoU-threshold comparisons concern empirical evaluation settings rather than new theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: The three central contributions—a data engine, comprehensive benchmark and grounding/referring model—remain intact. The revised introduction additionally claims that contemporary leading MLLMs struggle with basic document localization and recognition, emphasizing the benchmark's ability to expose these deficiencies.

C2.justification: v2 removes v1's explanations of missed grounding boxes in dense PDFs and vulnerability to changed inference resolution. It adds interpretations of competitors' coordinate-understanding weaknesses and attributes DOGR's remaining Ga F1 limitation to reasoning in Appendix F.3. New ablations receive explanations based on generator instruction-following and annotation precision, while Appendix C's existing failure cases remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds model-specific evaluation prompts, coordinate conversions, output-format rules, ablation construction details and manual hallucination-filtering information. It reports released code, data and model with a repository link instead of promising future release. Conversely, the explicit 20/16 inference-tile settings disappear; the main-text parsing-data count is corrected from 1.4M to 2.1M, already documented in v1's Figure 2 and appendix.

R1.justification: References are updated with newer Qwen, InternVL and Gemini reports, alongside additions such as PyMuPDF and removals of older background and baseline works. The central positioning relative to DocOwl-1.5, Kosmos-2.5 and Fox remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and several data-engine passages receive substantial rewriting. Section 6.2 is reorganized around basic capability verification, comparative evaluation and detailed model performance. The revision also renames DOGE throughout, changes author information, adds acknowledgements and inserts a new evaluation appendix before the existing supplementary experiments.

P2.justification: Benchmark statistics move from v1 Table 1 into a redesigned Figure 4. DocLocal4K results are redistributed across v2 Tables 1 and 4, Table 2 expands into a model comparison, Table 3 contracts and Table 5 is replaced. Figures 14–16 and Tables 9–10 are added. Most existing pipeline and qualitative illustrations remain, with a corrected explanatory label in Figure 12.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses a central weakness of v1: the proposed benchmark originally lacked competing-model results. Broad comparisons, documented evaluation prompts and controlled data-quality ablations substantially strengthen evidence for the benchmark and data engine. Removing the tile-sensitivity study and inference settings, leaving the benchmark revision underexplained and overstating the reasoning-only bottleneck weaken transparency. Nevertheless, the central empirical case is substantially better supported.
